chapters.goal: Rosie wants her slice of pie quickly

links.attempt: Rosie asks the diner for a pie
links.breaks: The diner has no oven: every app needs the same data, so it lives in one shared source of truth

links.attempt: Every slice is ordered from the farm
links.breaks: Each read is a slow database trip, and repeated reads of the same hot data overload it
links.source: Nishtala et al. NSDI 2013 s2, s3.2, s3.3

chapters.goal: Rosie wants today's pie, not last week's
chapters.from: price: the case keeps showing a pie after the farm changes the recipe

links.breaks: Freshness is a clock rule, so without expiry or invalidation a copy is stale with no limit

links.attempt: A date sticker (TTL) on each pie
links.breaks: Short TTL means constant refills and load; long TTL means long staleness

links.attempt: The Baker phones to throw out the pie (delete on write)
links.breaks: A slow refill can land after the delete and put the old value back (stale set)

chapters.goal: Rosie wants her favourite pie to still be there
chapters.from: price: the case is small, so it fills up

links.attempt: Keep every pie until its sticker runs out
links.breaks: Memory is bounded; at maxmemory with noeviction, writes are rejected with an OOM error
links.source: redis.io key eviction docs; Redis 7.4.0 src/server.c

links.attempt: Throw a pie out at random
links.breaks: A random victim can be the hottest key, so many readers miss

chapters.goal: Rosie wants pie even at noon
chapters.from: price: a popular pie's sticker runs out at the busiest hour

links.attempt: Every miss sends its own order
links.breaks: A hot key expiring makes many concurrent misses all recompute it, which slows each one and grows the pile
The stampede only moves to the next expiry, and data gets staler

links.attempt: Everyone waits on the spike for the one order
links.breaks: Every waiter still pays the full trip
